sentences.en: you see them walking away arrogantly.

parts.label: a
parts.ask: For each underlined phrase, tick ليست حالا if it is not a حال; if it is, tick حال and also tick the ruling for its واو حالية (منع الواو | جواز الواو | وجوب الواو).

questions.explanation:
The action of "seeing" was done upon them whilst they were "walking away". "They" performed the action of "walking away" whilst being "arrogant".
"Walking away", which is فعل مضارع مثبت without a قد, is a haal but will not have a waaw haaliyyah.
"Being arrogant" is also haal. And it requires a waaw haaliyah as it is a jumla ismiyyah beginning with a dhameer raabit.

parts.ask: For each underlined phrase, tick ليست حالا if it is not a حال; if it is, tick حال and also tick the ruling for its واو حالية (منع الواو | جواز الواو | وجوب الواو).

questions.explanation:
All of them are haal as they are all jumlas and neither of them need a waaw haaliyya as they all have a dhameer raabit.
The first for being فعل مضارع مثبت without a قد will not have a waaw haaliyya.
The second for being JIK which does not begin with the dhameer raabit, hence waaw haaliyya is optional.
The third for being فعل مضارع منفي with لا will not have a waaw haaliyya.

The second is a jumla which is a فعل مضارع مثبت without قد so will not have a waaw

sentences.ar: رَأيتُ مَنْ في المسجد مصلِّياً أو هُوَ جَالِسٌ
sentences.en: I saw the one who was in the masjid whilst praying or sitting.

parts.label: a
parts.ask: For each blue-underlined item, tick whether it is حال and, if so, which واو ruling applies.

questions.explanation:
"The one who was in the masjid" was either "praying" or "sitting".
Here, both are haal. The "sitting" does not take a waaw haaliyyah because it is mufrad and not a jumla, and the part after وl also does not require a waaw haaliyah because it is a jumla ismiyah beginning with the dhameer rabit and is ataf to a haal preceding it.

sentences.ar: تَرَى الْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي الأَصْفَادِ سَرَابِيلُهُمْ مِنْ قَطِرَانٍ وَتَغْشَىٰ وُجُوهَهُمُ ٱلنَّارُ
sentences.en: You will see the criminals that Day, bound together in irons, their garments of liquid pitch and their faces covered by the Fire.

parts.label: a

questions.explanation: The first does not take a waw haaliyah as it a -Mufrad Haal-; the second can take a waw haaliyah as it is a jumla ismiyah that has dhameer raabit but does not begin with it hence it's optional; and the last one does not take a waw haaliyah as it is a jumla with a فعل مضارع مثبت without a قد and has a dhameer raabit (The waw before it is actually for atf and not for haal).

questions.explanation: The action of "feeding the birds" was done while "throwing seeds at them" so it will be haal in tarkeeb. And since it has a فعل مضارع مثبت with it's ma'mool preceding it, a waaw haaliyyah is optional but not necessary.

sentences.en: No new revelation comes to them from their Lord except that they listen to it playfully, their hearts distracted.

parts.label: a
parts.ask: For each blue-underlined item, tick whether it is حال, and if so tick the applicable واو حالية ruling (منع الواو | جواز الواو | وجوب الواو); if not حال tick ليست حالا.

questions.explanation:
All three are haal because that is "their" state when "they" receive the revelation.
The first one does not take a waaw haaliyyah because it is a فعل ماضي which comes after إلا.
The second one requires a waaw haaliyyah because it is a jumla ismiyyah beginning with the dhameer raabit.
The third one does not take waaw haaliyah because it is a mufrad haal and not a jumla.

sentences.ar: مَا لَكُمْ لا تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ لِتُؤْمِنُوا بِرَبِّكُمْ وَقَدْ أَخَذَ مِيثَاقَكُمْ
sentences.en: What is the matter with you that you do not believe in God when the Messenger calls you to believe in your Lord, and He has already made a pledge with you, if you have faith?

parts.label: a
parts.ask: For each blue-underlined clause, is it a حال? If so, tick the ruling for the واو حالية.

questions.explanation:
All of them can be taken as haal in tarkeeb as "you" are in the state that "you do not believe in....". The first one doesn't take a waaw haaliyah because it's a فعل مضارع منفي with a dhameer raabit.
The second one is a jumlah ismiyyah which does not cotain a dhameer raabit, hence the waaw haaliyyah is necessary.
The third one is also optional because it is a فعل ماضي with a dhameer raabit.

sentences.ar: أَتُحَاجُّونِّي فِي اللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدَانِي وَلَا أَخَافُ مَا تُشْرِكُونَ بِهِ
sentences.en: How can you argue with me about God when He has guided me? I do not fear anything you associate with Him.

parts.label: a
parts.ask: For each clause, decide if it is حال; if it is, tick the ruling for the واو حالية.

questions.explanation:
First one is haal because when "You" are arguing with me, the state "I" am in is that "Allah has guided me". And since the first one is فعل ماضي with a dhameer raabit, the "Yaa" in 'Hadanee', it is persimmable for it to have a waaw haaliyah.
As for the second part, that also comes under the haaliyyah sentence. Since it is a فعل مضارع منفي with لا, it cannot take a waaw haaliyah, therefore the waaw before it is atifa making it معطوف to the haal before it. It is NOT an independent haal.
